review_scope: Reviewed all 6 sparse contact-sheet pages covering 137 frames sampled every 45 seconds and all 25 dense contact-sheet pages sampled every 10 seconds. This remains a still-frame visual screening, not continuous audiovisual verification.

observations.description: Mikey appears alone at the desk while a vertically cropped phone/profile interface is displayed beside him; the phone content is part of the live explanation.

A sequence of private-message screenshots begins, including contact/profile pages, green and grey message bubbles, images, and visible voice-message entries. The displayed sequence changes repeatedly.
The phone panel switches through a blurred photo feed/profile view and a long Chinese text post or comment page before returning to chat screens.

Messaging screenshots show alternating participants, decorative stickers, screenshots within the conversation, and multiple voice-message controls. Message order and sender side carry the case meaning.

Ten-second frames show a blurred young man continuously in the full-height phone view from about 43:50 to 48:10, with a second darker face visible in a small inset at about 46:00 and 47:30. This is visually consistent with a video-call or call-recording display, but the identities, audio, and live-versus-prerecorded status remain unresolved.
A photographed paper/form with rows and handwritten or printed details is shown in the phone content, followed by further private chats and embedded images.

Long messaging runs contain numerous voice-message bubbles, highlighted message screenshots, a PDF/file-like attachment, photos, and long text blocks; audio playback cannot be confirmed from still frames.
The displayed thread includes explicit time markers and call-duration style entries. These may support chronology but require closer frames and audio context before interpreting outcomes.
Later chat screens include photos and video/voice previews from third parties while Mikey continues commenting on them.

dense_review_windows.reason: Read profile/interface details and determine how the opening case is introduced; sparse frames do not preserve scrolling or exact screen changes.
Private chat sequence with message order, voice entries, sender identity, and possible result claims.
Profile/feed and long-text post transitions carry content that cannot be reconstructed from 45-second samples.
Multiple chats, stickers, images, apparent video-call/selfie material, and a document/form require denser sequential frames.
Extended private-message walkthrough containing highlighted bubbles, voice messages, call/timestamp records, attachments, and long text.
Final case/chat sequence includes third-party images and voice/video previews; end boundary should be checked against the source duration.

attribution_limits: The studio speaker is visually consistent with Mikey, but text in the phone screenshots belongs to multiple chat participants and must not be attributed to him without sender-side verification.
Voice-message and video/call previews are visible, but sparse stills cannot establish whether they were played, who spoke, or whether Mikey quoted, paraphrased, endorsed, or criticized them.
A displayed screenshot may be an actual case, an example, a repost, or a critique; the visual screen alone does not prove its status.
The blurred young man and the second inset face shown around 43:50-48:10 are third parties; no identity or statement attribution can be inferred from the still frames.
privacy_or_third_party_risks: Private chats expose participant avatars, message text, timestamps, images, call records, voice-message controls, and possible account identifiers.
A third-party face is visible in the phone video/selfie sequence even though it is blurred.
The photographed form/document may contain personal or transactional details and requires redaction review before reuse.
Third-party photos, video previews, and attachments must remain research evidence unless individually cleared and de-identified.

dense_observations.description: From about 16:50, ten-second frames preserve a long dark chat sequence with alternating green and grey sender sides, images, voice-message shapes, and call-duration-like entries. Sender-side changes are visible, but participant identities are not.

From about 43:50 to 48:10 the phone panel repeatedly shows a blurred young man's face; two sampled moments also show a second face in a small inset. The visual layout supports a call-like display but does not establish that the call was live or that its audio was heard in the stream.

Around 55:10-57:50 a highlighted voice-message or audio-like item remains visible while Mikey comments. The sampled controls do not show a reliable progress change, so playback and speaker identity are unconfirmed.

The later chat sequence contains a file/PDF-like attachment, photos, call-duration or time indicators, vehicle images, and video/voice previews. The ten-second ordering improves chronology but does not prove the asserted relationship or outcome of the case.

Late frames show additional third-party photographs, including women, and further video previews inside the private thread; these are source materials rather than visually attributable statements by Mikey.

remaining_visual_limits: The dense review samples one still every 10 seconds; it is not continuous audiovisual verification and may miss brief scrolls, taps, cuts, refusals, consent, or playback state changes between samples.
Small, blurred, or partially cropped chat text cannot be transcribed reliably from the contact sheets, so exact wording and message order still require source-level checking.
Visible voice and video controls do not establish that media was played or audible, and faces or sender sides do not establish participant identity.
No consent, refusal, behavioral result, or causal outcome is visually proven by the sampled frames alone.
